name: Moravel Passionfruit-Szechuan Cola
description: A dark cola base layered with synth-passionfruit and a numbing Szechuan pepper finish — an unusual combination that polarizes drinkers but builds fierce loyalty among those it hooks.
flavor_profile: Sweet cola entry, tropical passionfruit mid-note, then a mild lip-tingling Szechuan numbness that lingers
cultural_context: Moravel occupies a cult position — too weird for mass adoption, too good for its fans to abandon. It's the drink people bring to parties to prove something about themselves. Augmented users note the Szechuan tingle interacts oddly with certain sensory implants.
story_hooks: A neurosensory researcher is quietly studying whether Moravel's Szechuan compound produces measurable effects in users with tactile augmentation — she hasn't published because the results are stranger than expected.
Moravel is hemorrhaging money and the founder is considering selling the formula to a megacorp, which would inevitably strip the real Szechuan pepper from the recipe — fans are organizing.
Someone has been using the Moravel brand logo — a stylized nerve ending — as a gang identifier in the eastern Shelf corridors, and it's causing legal headaches for the company.
